title: Prompting like a tool, briefing like a colleague
heading: One line against a first day
caption: You would never brief a person in one line.

last-year.text: What worked, and what did not.

access.text: Booking system, catering contacts, the calendar.

ask.text: One structured plan for the CEO, by end of day.

check.text: I review the draft at three. Every number gets a source.

unstated-requirements-are-guessed.description: Models infer a missing requirement correctly only about 41% of the time, and underspecified prompts are twice as likely to regress when the model or prompt changes.[1]

what-prompts-dont-say.title: Yang, Shi, Ma, Liu, Kästner, Wu, What Prompts Don’t Say: Understanding and Managing Underspecification in LLM Prompts

say-it-up-front.description: Across more than 200,000 simulated conversations, every tested model did worse when a task arrived underspecified over several turns than when fully specified at once, by 39% on average.[1]

lost-in-multi-turn.title: Laban, Hayashi, Zhou, Neville, LLMs Get Lost In Multi-Turn Conversation

relevant-specific-context.description: Handing a model the one relevant document lifted question-answering accuracy for GPT-3.5-Turbo from 56.1% to 88.3%, a 2023 retrieval result whose direction transfers and whose size does not. With 20 or 30 documents it could fall below having none.[1] Anthropic: “minimal does not necessarily mean short”.[2] Measured evidence for a human-written brief in non-coding knowledge work is thin.

lost-in-the-middle.title: Liu et al., Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts, TACL 2024, Table 1 and section 2.3

effective-context-engineering.title: Anthropic, Effective context engineering for AI agents

back-to-the-hook.title: Back to the hook
back-to-the-hook.keywords: the gap, the question left hanging, one line, Plan our Sommerfest
back-to-the-hook.script: Now back to the hook. Remember the gap, and the question I left hanging? Think about the last thing you typed into an AI. It was probably one line. Plan our Sommerfest. You would never brief a person like that.

the-answer-to-the-hanging-why.title: The answer to the hanging why
the-answer-to-the-hanging-why.keywords: prompt it like a tool, onboard it like a colleague, a management task, different skills
the-answer-to-the-hanging-why.script: So here is my answer. AI underdelivers when you prompt it like a tool, and the real job is to onboard it like a colleague. And onboarding is a management task, not an execution one. It needs different skills than typing does.
